first.rationale: Verify the two highest-consequence competing levers: promotional pricing addresses the acute competitive loss but may trade durable qualified revenue for discounted, lower-value acquisition; onboarding simplification directly addresses declining completion and has a prior durable activation signal. Pending source review, run a guarded onboarding simplification test with qualified-revenue and downstream retention guardrails rather than assume acquisition lift is sustainable value.

mid.rationale: Run a guarded SMB onboarding-simplification experiment, prioritizing removal or deferral of nonessential signup/onboarding steps. The verified SMB result showed activation +9%, qualified revenue +4%, and only a -1% 30-day retention change, while current completion and activation are both declining. Do not use promotional pricing: its verified +18% qualified-revenue lift came with -12% 30-day retention and is explicitly unsuitable for sustainable growth. Keep the test SMB-scoped because the verified simplification result was not replicated beyond SMB; monitor qualified revenue, activation, onboarding completion, and 30-day retention before expanding.

final2.rationale: Keep the SMB onboarding-simplification experiment. The deeper competitor cut and doubled price-driven churn make a pricing response urgent, but the verified targeted-discount result is specifically inconsistent with the objective: it produced -12% 30-day retention and was concluded not to be sustainable growth. Verified SMB simplification improved activation (+9%) and qualified revenue (+4%) with only a -1% 30-day retention change, while both onboarding completion and activation are currently declining. Scope the test to SMB and use retention, qualified revenue, and churn guardrails; do not infer that improved onboarding alone offsets price-driven churn.
